what_its_for: Droxidopa is used to treat dizziness, lightheadedness, and fainting that happens when you stand up (called neurogenic orthostatic hypotension, or nOH). This is caused by certain nervous system conditions like Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy, or pure autonomic failure. The medicine helps raise your blood pressure when you stand up so you feel less dizzy and more steady.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a glass of water. You can take droxidopa with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Take your last dose of the day at least 3 hours before bedtime. This is very important because droxidopa can raise your blood pressure too much while you are lying down (called supine hypertension), which is dangerous during sleep. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsules unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose of 100 mg taken 3 times a day (morning, midday, and late afternoon). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose every 24 to 48 hours until your symptoms are well controlled. The usual dose range is 100 mg to 600 mg taken 3 times a day. Do not take more than 1,800 mg total in one day. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is not too close to bedtime. Remember, you must take your last dose at least 3 hours before you go to sleep. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store droxidopa at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place — not in the bathroom. Keep the medicine in its original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not lie flat or sleep shortly after taking a dose — always wait at least 3 hours after your last daily dose before lying down or going to bed, as this can cause dangerously high blood pressure while lying down. Avoid alcohol, as it can worsen dizziness or low blood pressure. Avoid standing up too quickly, especially when getting out of bed or a chair. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or supplements, especially other medicines that raise blood pressure or stimulants. Avoid caffeine if your doctor advises it, as it can sometimes add to blood pressure effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: a severe headache, vision changes (blurring, spots, or vision loss), chest pain, shortness of breath, or pounding heartbeat — these may be signs of dangerously high blood pressure. Also call your doctor if you notice: worsening dizziness or fainting, severe nausea or vomiting, unusual confusion or behavior changes, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Tell your doctor if the medicine does not seem to be helping your symptoms after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Droxidopa usually starts to work within a few hours of the first dose, but it may take a few days or up to 2 weeks to notice the full benefit. Your doctor will check in with you regularly to see how well it is working and to adjust your dose if needed. Because your body may respond differently over time, your doctor may periodically reassess whether the medicine is still helping you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if droxidopa is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Older adults (seniors): Older patients may be more sensitive to blood pressure changes and side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely and may start with a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: Droxidopa has not been studied in children and is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old.
